relationships.subject: CXCL13
relationships.evidence_quote: CXCL13 binds with CXCR5 to initiate several key intracellular signaling, including ERK, JNK and NF-κB pathway, etc. [16, 45, 46].

relationships.subject: STAT3
relationships.evidence_quote: These data indicate that STAT3 activation contributes to the upregulation of CXCL13 in SCDH and mechanical allodynia of CPIP mice.

relationships.subject: CXCL13
relationships.evidence_quote: Neutralizing CXCL13 in spinal cord significantly ameliorated bilateral mechanical allodynia of CPIP mice compared with isotype control IgG (Fig. 3B, C).

relationships.subject: CXCR5
relationships.evidence_quote: This result indicates that spinal pNF-κB is a downstream signaling of CXCR5 in the context of CPIP.

relationships.subject: NF-κB
relationships.evidence_quote: Among these genes, the expression of Il6 was significantly reduced by PDTC treatment (Fig. 8E), indicating the expression of these two genes were regulated by NF-κB.

relationships.subject: IL-6
relationships.evidence_quote: Spinal blocking IL-6 significantly alleviated mechanical allodynia of CPIP mice compared with vehicle control at time points we observed (Fig. 8H).

key_findings: Spinal neuronal CXCL13/CXCR5 signaling drives NF-κB activation, Il6 upregulation and mechanical allodynia in the CPIP model of CRPS-I; STAT3 promotes CXCL13 upregulation.
